inputs.notes: Balance sheet as of Q3 FY2026 (March 31, 2026). Cash $1,136.3M (all cash; company liquidated short-term investments and deployed ~$991M in buybacks in Q3). Total Debt $989.1M (senior notes: $500M 5.25% due 2029 + $500M 5.5% due 2034, net of discount/issuance costs). Net Debt = Debt - Cash = -$147.2M (net cash position: cash slightly exceeds debt by $147M — a significant swing from the prior model's net cash of $577M, driven by the $991M Q3 buyback). Shares outstanding 261.0M (down from 263.8M; management guides ~2.5% decrease in diluted share count for FY26). Last FCF is FY2025 full-year free cash flow of $1,415.5M. TTM FCF (Q4FY25 + Q1-Q3FY26) = $1,204.7M is lower due to Q1/Q2 FY26 being lighter FCF quarters; FY2025 annual figure is more representative of sustainable run-rate and is used as the base.

historical_growth.eps_note: GAAP EPS negative throughout due to heavy SBC (~23-25% of revenue). Cannot compute meaningful CAGR. EPS improved in magnitude from -$2.05 (FY2022) to -$0.98 (FY2025) but remains negative. Q3 FY26 restructuring charges ($224M) further suppress near-term GAAP EPS. FCF used as primary profitability metric per project instructions.
historical_growth.equity_note: Equity 3Y CAGR is unusually high (60%) due to the artificially depressed FY2022 equity base ($327M) from GAAP net losses and SBC. Q3 FY2026 equity fell sharply to $879M from $1,591M in Q2 due to $991M of buybacks. Equity CAGR is unreliable and not used as the primary rate.
historical_growth.growth_rate_rationale: Per company-specific instructions, FCF CAGR is the primary metric for TEAM (not equity CAGR), as GAAP net losses from SBC make equity growth unreliable. The FCF 3-year CAGR of 23.6% aligns closely with revenue growth (23.0% 3Y CAGR) and management's raised FY26 guidance of ~24% total revenue growth. Q3 FY26 Cloud growth accelerated to 29% YoY, and management guided non-GAAP operating margin to 29% for FY26 (34% in Q3 alone), reinforcing that FCF growth can sustain above this rate near-term. The FCF 3-year CAGR of 23.6% is selected as the representative growth rate, with scenarios modeled above and below this.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3Y CAGR (60.2%) diverges significantly from Revenue 3Y CAGR (23.0%) — gap of 37.2pp. This is due to the artificially depressed FY2022 equity base ($327M) from GAAP net losses. Equity CAGR is not used for DCF; FCF CAGR is the selected primary metric. No divergence concern between FCF and Revenue CAGRs (0.6pp gap). Note: equity fell sharply in Q3 FY26 to $879M due to $991M buybacks, further distorting any equity-based growth metric.

base.description: ~22% FCF growth in Year 1 (consistent with management's raised FY26 revenue guidance of ~24% and non-GAAP operating margin of 29%), decelerating to 10% by Year 5 as the Data Center revenue cliff materializes in FY27 (management explicitly warned of meaningful DC deceleration) and Cloud growth normalizes. FCF grows slightly faster than revenue due to margin expansion from 27% to ~30%+ as restructuring savings (10% headcount cut) are realized and reinvested more selectively. WACC 10% appropriate for high-growth enterprise SaaS with improving FCF but ongoing SBC dilution mitigation via buybacks.

bull.description: Cloud acceleration sustained at 25%+ through FY28 driven by DC-to-Cloud migration multi-year tailwind, Rovo/AI monetization kicking in (customers using Rovo are growing ARR at 2x the rate of non-Rovo customers), Service Collection scaling past $1B ARR at 30%+ growth, and enterprise RPO ($4.0B, +37% YoY) providing multi-year revenue visibility. Restructuring creates structurally higher margins (Q3 FY26 non-GAAP margin hit 34%, 8ppts above prior year), and aggressive buybacks ($2.2B remaining authorization) shrink share count further. FCF growth 28% Y1 declining to 14% Y5. Lower WACC reflects reduced risk as cloud mix exceeds 80%, enterprise commitments deepen, and capital return program is established. Aligns with bull case: Teamwork Graph as AI data moat, agentic automation flywheel, largest-ever competitive ITSM displacements in Q3 FY26.

bear.description: Data Center revenue cliff in FY27 creates a visible near-term headwind as EOL recognition pull-forward unwinds (DC guided to only 8.5% growth in Q4 FY26 after 44% in Q3; management flagged meaningful deceleration in FY27). Microsoft bundling intensifies across Azure DevOps/GitHub/Copilot, pressuring developer-team retention. Enterprise GTM transition stumbles under dual leadership transitions (President seat vacant since Dec 2025, new CFO James Chuong still in learning phase). FCF growth moderates to 14% Y1 declining to 4% Y5. Higher WACC (12%) reflects elevated execution risk. FCF margin remains flat at 25% as AI infrastructure costs (Rovo compute growing 20%+ MoM) and enterprise sales build absorb restructuring savings. Aligns with bear case: DC revenue cliff, GTM transition risk, software multiple compression, AI monetization still nascent relative to investment.

sensitivity.note: Matrix uses base case FCF growth rates [22%, 19%, 16%, 13%, 10%] applied from FY2025 FCF of $1,415.5M. Net cash of $147.2M added to equity value (less_net_debt = -147.2). Shares outstanding 261.0M. All values in USD per share.

sanity_check.diagnosis: No over-valuation flags triggered. Stock trades at 3.97x P/Sales, well below its entire 10-year historical P/Sales range of 10.2x-30.7x (average 18.1x). Base-case upside of 73.8% is below the 100% threshold. Current price of $79.26 sits in the lower portion of the 10-year price range ($24-$458, midpoint ~$241). No peak-FCF extrapolation concern — FCF is genuinely growing (Q3 FY26 FCF was $561M, 31% margin). All checks pass.

implied_multiples.note: P/Sales computed using FY2025 revenue of $5,215.3M. IV-implied P/Sales at base case (6.89x) and bull case (10.74x) are both at or below the 10-year historical minimum of 10.2x (FY2025 actual). Bear IV implies 3.80x P/Sales, suggesting the bear case prices in further multiple compression below any observed historical level.

historical_anchors.rationale: P/E is N/A — GAAP EPS has been negative every fiscal year due to SBC expense of 23-27% of revenue. P/B is not a meaningful anchor — equity has ranged from $294M to $1,591M and is now distorted by $991M of Q3 FY26 buybacks, resulting in historical P/B of 8.7x-217x with no consistent pattern. P/Sales is the most reliable historical valuation anchor for TEAM.
historical_anchors.vs_history: Current P/Sales of 3.97x is BELOW the 10-year minimum of 10.2x (FY2025 at the prior trough). The stock has re-rated dramatically from 30.7x (FY2021 peak) to levels not observed in the historical dataset, reflecting: (a) software multiple compression broadly, (b) post-ZIRP discount rate normalization, and (c) near-term concern about the FY27 Data Center revenue cliff.

fcf_quality_check.assessment: FCF is genuine and growing — not cyclically elevated. FY2025 FCF of $1,415.5M represents a 23.6% 3-year CAGR from FY2022. Q3 FY26 FCF of $561M (31% margin) confirms continued momentum. FCF margin has expanded from 27% (FY2025) as restructuring reduces opex. No mean-reversion concern warranted.

pe_trip_test.reason: GAAP EPS has been negative every fiscal year throughout the history of the company as a listed US public entity (FY2022: -$2.05, FY2023: -$1.90, FY2024: -$1.16, FY2025: -$0.98). SBC expense of $1.2-1.4B annually drives GAAP losses. Q4 FY26 is guided to 4.5% GAAP operating margin — potentially approaching breakeven on a trailing-twelve-month basis going into FY27, but no reliable EPS anchor exists for valuation trip testing.

pb_trip_test.reason: Book value is severely distorted by (1) accumulated GAAP net losses driven by SBC, and (2) $991M Q3 FY26 buybacks reducing equity to $879M as of March 2026. Historical P/B has ranged from 8.7x to 217x with no consistent pattern. Not a meaningful valuation anchor for TEAM.

key_investment_considerations.primary_value_driver: Cloud migration and expanding FCF margins. TEAM generated $1.4B FCF on $5.2B revenue (27% margin) in FY2025. Cloud growth accelerated to 29% YoY in Q3 FY26 (above the 25-26% range seen in prior quarters). The 2029 Data Center EOL deadline creates a multi-year structural tailwind for cloud growth, with 9-month FY26 FCF already at $844M. The Q3 FY26 restructuring (10% headcount cut, $224M charges) is generating structural margin improvement, with non-GAAP operating margin reaching 34% in Q3 FY26 versus 26% a year prior.
key_investment_considerations.key_risk: Data Center revenue cliff in FY27 — management explicitly flagged meaningful deceleration as the FY26 EOL recognition pull-forward (worth ~11.5pp of DC growth in FY26, with DC already guided to only 8.5% in Q4 FY26 after 44% in Q3) unwinds. Simultaneously managing a major restructuring (10% headcount, 900+ R&D roles) and dual leadership transitions (President seat vacant since Dec 2025; new CFO James Chuong in seat since March 30, 2026). $1.6B of acquisitions (DX, The Browser Company) must integrate and deliver ROI.
key_investment_considerations.current_price_assessment: At $79.26 (June 30, 2026), TEAM trades at 3.97x trailing P/Sales — below its own 10-year minimum of 10.2x. The stock sits in the lower quarter of its 10-year range ($24-$458). Even using conservative base-case assumptions (FCF growth decelerating from 22% to 10% over 5 years), intrinsic value is $137.77, implying 74% upside. The $79.26 price is below the base-case entry price for a 15% CAGR target ($83.05), meaning an investor today is priced to earn above 15% annually even under the base case. The bear-case IV ($75.84) is the only scenario where the current price appears fair or above intrinsic value, and that scenario requires material execution failure. The probability-weighted IV of $141.52 implies 79% upside. The balance sheet has shifted from $577M net cash (prior model) to $147M net cash after aggressive Q3 buybacks ($991M), which is a positive capital allocation signal but marginally reduces the floor value.
key_investment_considerations.moat_assessment: Strong switching costs via Jira/Confluence workflow embedding, proprietary Teamwork Graph (100B+ objects connecting work, knowledge, people, and code) as AI data moat, Marketplace ecosystem network effects, and now MCP Gallery enabling third-party agents to plug into the Teamwork Graph. These factors support above-average terminal growth rate assumptions. Q3 FY26 was Atlassian's largest-ever quarter for competitive ITSM displacements, and Rovo customers are growing ARR at 2x the rate of non-Rovo customers — early but concrete evidence of AI-enhanced moat.
key_investment_considerations.wacc_rationale: 10% base WACC reflects: risk-free rate ~4.3%, equity risk premium ~5%, beta ~1.1 for high-growth enterprise SaaS. Lower WACC (9%) in bull case as cloud mix approaches 80%, enterprise multi-year commitments deepen (RPO $4.0B, +37% YoY), and capital return program ($2.2B authorization remaining) reduces equity risk. Higher WACC (12%) in bear case for elevated execution risk during simultaneous restructuring, leadership transitions, and GTM model shift from PLG to enterprise direct sales.
